source_text: ἀληθῆ περιμένων πεῦσιν· ἐπειδὴ δὲ διεγηγερμένος, δύο κλάδους ἐλαιῶν ὠνόμαζε λοιπὸν, καὶ ἀναμαθεῖν ἐλιπάρει, τίνος ἂν εἴη σύμβολα ταυτὶ ἐδιδάσκετο παραχρῆμα, τοῦ ἀγγέλου λέγοντος· «Οὗτοι οἱ δύο υἱοὶ τῆς πιότητος παρεστήκασι τῷ Κυρίῳ πάσης τῆς γῆς.» Υἱοὺς δὲ πιότητος δύο, τόν τε ἐξ Ἰσραὴλ, καὶ μέν τοι τὸν ἐξ ἐθνῶν ἀπεκάλει λαὸν, οὓς καὶ τῷ Κυρίῳ πάσης τῆς γῆς παρεστάναι φησὶ, σαφῶς τε καὶ ἐναργῶς εἰς τύπον Χριστοῦ, τὸ ἐπὶ τῇ λυχνίᾳ τέχνημα τιθεὶς, ἧς οἱ κλάδοι τῶν ἐλαιῶν, εἰς δεξιά τε καὶ εὐώνυμα, καὶ οἱονεὶ τὴν ἐν κύκλῳ λαχόντες στάσιν τῷ ἐλαίῳ καταπιαίνονται, ὅ ἐστιν ἁγίου Πνεύματος τύπος, τὸν τῶν πιστευόντων κατάρδοντος νοῦν, κατὰ τὸ, «Ἐν ἐλαίῳ ἐλίπανας τὴν κεφαλήν μου.» {ΠΑΛΛ.} Εἶτα τί μὴ μᾶλλον ἐλαίας αὐτὰς, κλῶνας δὲ μᾶλλον ἐλαιῶν ἀπεκάλει; {ΚΥΡ.} Ὅτι, ὦ ἑταῖρε, καθάπερ ἐξ ἐλαιῶν μόσχια λεπτὰ καὶ ἀρτιθαλεῖς ἐξῄρηνται κλάδοι, μόνον δὲ οὐχὶ μεταβοθρεύονται μετὰ πίστεως εἰς εὐσέβειαν οἱ πεπιστευκότες, οἱ μὲν ἐκ τῆς Ἰουδαίων ὄντες συναγωγῆς, οἱ δὲ, τῆς ἐξ ἐθνῶν πληθύος ἐξῃρημένοι· πεπιστεύκασι γὰρ οὐχὶ πάντες οἱ ἐξ Ἰσραὴλ, οὔτε μὴν ἅπασα τῶν ἐθνῶν εἰσέφρησεν ἡ πληθύς. Κλάδοι τοίνυν ἐλαιῶν, οἱ ὡς ἐκ δένδρων ἀπεσπασμένοι πληθύος Ἰουδαϊκῆς, καὶ μὴν καὶ Ἑλληνικῆς, καὶ ἐν φωτὶ τῷ θείῳ γεγενημένοι, καὶ ἐνσπαταλῶντες ἤδη πως τῇ τοῦ ἁγίου Πνεύματος ἀφθονωτέρᾳ χύσει. Τοῦτο γὰρ οἶμαι δηλοῦν, τὸ, ὡς ἐν μυξωτῆρσι τῶν λύχνων τοὺς τῶν ἐλαιῶν κεῖσθαι κλάδους, ὧν καὶ ὁ μακάριος Ψαλμῳδὸς διαμέμνηταί που, πρὸς τὸν τῶν ὅλων Σωτῆρα Χριστὸν ἀναμελῳδῶν τε καὶ λέγων περί τε τῆς συνηρμοσμένης αὐτῷ νύμφης, τουτέστι, τῆς Ἐκκλησίας, καὶ τῶν ἐν πίστει τέκνων αὐτῆς· «Ἡ γυνή σου ὡς ἄμπελος εὐθηνοῦσα ἐν τοῖς κλίτεσι τῆς οἰκίας σου. Οἱ υἱοί σου, ὡς νεόφυτα ἐλαιῶν κύκλῳ τῆς τραπέζης σου.» Ζωοποιούμεθα γὰρ ἐν μεθέξει Πνεύματος, καὶ ἐν ἁγίᾳ τραπέζῃ Χριστοῦ, τὴν εἰς αὐτὸν πίστιν εἰσδεδεγμένοι. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Ναὶ λέγεις ὀρθῶς· «Ἐγὼ γάρ εἰμι,» φησὶν, «ὁ ἄρτος ὁ ζῶν, ὁ ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καταβὰς, καὶ ζωὴν διδοὺς τῷ κόσμῳ.» {ΚΥΡ.} Ἀλλὰ λυχνίας μὲν πέρι, καὶ τῶν ἐν αὐτῇ, ταυτὶ πρὸς ἡμῶν εἰς παρὸν εἰρήσεται. Ἴτω δὲ ὁ λόγος ἐπὶ τὸ χαλκοῦν ἤδη θυσιαστήριον, τῆς κατὰ νόμον λατρείας, τὸ χρειωδέστατον. «Ποιήσεις γὰρ,» φησὶ, «θυσιαστήριον ἐκ ξύλων ἀσήπτων. Πέντε πήχεων τὸ μῆκος, καὶ πέντε πήχεων τὸ εὖρος. Τετράγωνον ἔσται τὸ θυσιαστήριον, καὶ τριῶν πήχεων τὸ ὕψος αὐτοῦ· καὶ ποιήσεις τὰ κέρατα ἐπὶ τῶν τεσσάρων γωνιῶν, ἐξ αὐτοῦ ἔσται τὰ κέρατα, καὶ καλύψεις αὐτὰ χαλκῷ, καὶ ποιήσεις στεφάνην τῷ θυσιαστηρίῳ, καὶ τὸν καλυπτῆρα αὐτοῦ, καὶ τὰς φιάλας αὐτοῦ, καὶ τὰς κρεάγρας αὐτοῦ, καὶ τὸ πυρεῖον αὐτοῦ, πάντα τὰ σκεύη αὐτοῦ ποιήσεις χαλκᾶ.» Πεντάπηχυ μὲν οὖν εἰς εὖρός τε καὶ μῆκος
pass_a_gloss: [Cont. from s.12: ...awaiting the more sensible and] true inquiry (πεῦσις); but when, having been roused (διεγηγερμένος), he named at last two branches of olives and begged (ἐλιπάρει) to learn again of what these might be symbols (σύμβολα), he was taught at once (παραχρῆμα), the angel saying: These are the two sons of fatness; they stand by the Lord of all the earth. | Two sons of fatness he called the people from Israel and the people from the nations (ἐθνῶν), whom he says stand by (παρεστάναι) the Lord of all the earth, clearly and vividly (ἐναργῶς) setting (τιθείς) the artifice (τέχνημα) on the lampstand as a type (τύπος) of Christ, whose olive branches, to right and left, and as it were having obtained the position in a circle (ἐν κύκλῳ στάσιν), are fattened (καταπιαίνονται) with the oil (ἔλαιον), which is a type of the Holy Spirit watering (κατάρδοντος) the mind (νοῦς) of those believing, according to: In oil you fattened/anointed (ἐλίπανας) my head. | PALL.: Then why did he not rather call them olives, but rather sprigs of olives? | CYR.: Because, friend (ἑταῖρε), just as slender shoots (μόσχια λεπτά) and fresh-sprouted (ἀρτιθαλεῖς) branches are taken out (ἐξῄρηνται) from olives, so the believers are all but transplanted (μεταβοθρεύονται) with faith into piety (εὐσέβεια), some being from the synagogue (συναγωγή) of the Jews, others taken out from the multitude (πληθύς) of the nations; for not all from Israel have believed, nor did the whole multitude of the nations come in (εἰσέφρησεν). Branches of olives, then, are those torn off (ἀπεσπασμένοι) as from trees from the Jewish and also Greek (Ἑλληνικῆς) multitude, and having come to be in the divine light, and already somehow luxuriating (ἐνσπαταλῶντες) in the more abundant (ἀφθονωτέρᾳ) pouring (χύσις) of the Holy Spirit. For this I think is shown by the olive branches lying as in the nozzles (μυξωτῆρσι) of the lamps; of whom the blessed Psalmist (Ψαλμῳδός) makes mention somewhere, singing (ἀναμελῳδῶν) to Christ, Savior of all, and speaking about the bride (νύμφη) fitted to him (συνηρμοσμένης), that is, the Church, and her children in faith: [Ps 127:3 LXX] Your wife as a flourishing (εὐθηνοῦσα) vine on the sides (κλίτεσι) of your house; your sons as new plantings (νεόφυτα) of olives around your table (τράπεζα). For we are made alive (ζωοποιούμεθα) in participation (μέθεξις) of the Spirit and at the holy table of Christ, having received (εἰσδεδεγμένοι) faith in him. | PALL.: Yes, you say rightly: I am, he says, the living bread, which came down from heaven, and giving life to the world. | CYR.: But about the lampstand and the things in it, these things will be said by us for the present (εἰς παρόν). Let the discourse go now to the bronze (χαλκοῦν) altar (θυσιαστήριον), the most necessary (χρειωδέστατον) of the worship (λατρεία) according to law. [Exod 27:1-3] You shall make an altar from unrotting (ἀσήπτων) woods; five cubits (πήχεις) length, five breadth; square (τετράγωνον); three cubits height; horns (κέρατα) on the four corners; from it shall be the horns; cover (καλύψεις) them with bronze; make a crown (στεφάνη) for the altar, and its cover (καλυπτήρ), bowls (φιάλαι), flesh-hooks (κρεάγραι), fire-pan (πυρεῖον); all its vessels (σκεύη) bronze. | Five-cubit (πεντάπηχυ) then in breadth and length [cont. s.14]
pass_b_english: Cyril: …true question. But when, now roused, he at last named them two branches of olive trees and begged earnestly to learn what these might be symbols of, he was taught at once, when the angel said: ‘These are the two sons of richness, who stand beside the Lord of all the earth’ (Zechariah 4:14). By the two sons of richness he meant the people from Israel and also the people from the nations, who, he says, stand beside the Lord of all the earth. So he clearly and plainly sets the craftsmanship of the lampstand as a type of Christ. Its olive branches, on the right and on the left, having as it were their place all around it, are made rich with the oil, which is a type of the Holy Spirit, who waters the mind of those who believe, as it says: ‘You have anointed my head with oil’ (Psalm 23:5).
Palladius: Then why did he call them shoots of olive trees, and not rather olive trees?

Cyril: Because, my friend, those who have believed have been taken like slender shoots and newly sprouted branches from olive trees, and are all but transplanted, with faith, into godliness: some of them come from the synagogue of the Jews, and others have been taken out of the multitude of the nations. For not all those from Israel have believed, nor has the whole multitude of the nations come in. Branches of olive trees, then, are those who have been plucked, as from trees, from the multitude of the Jews and also of the Greeks, who have come to be in the divine light and already in some way delight in the more abundant outpouring of the Holy Spirit. For this, I think, is what is meant by the olive branches lying, as it were, in the spouts of the lamps. The blessed Psalmist also mentions them somewhere, singing to Christ, the Savior of all, and speaking of the bride joined to him, that is, the Church, and of her children in faith: ‘Your wife is like a flourishing vine on the sides of your house; your sons are like young olive plants around your table’ (Psalm 128:3). For we are given life by sharing in the Spirit and at the holy table of Christ, once we have received faith in him.
Palladius: Yes, you are right. For he says, ‘I am the living bread that came down from heaven and gives life to the world’ (John 6:33, 51).

Cyril: But let this be what we say for the present about the lampstand and the things on it. Let our discussion now go on to the bronze altar, the most necessary thing in the worship under the law. For he says: ‘You shall make an altar of wood that does not rot, five cubits long and five cubits wide. The altar shall be square, and its height three cubits. And you shall make the horns on the four corners; the horns shall be of one piece with it, and you shall cover them with bronze. And you shall make a crown for the altar, and its cover, and its bowls, and its meat forks, and its firepan; all its vessels you shall make of bronze.’ (Exodus 27:1–3) Now, five cubits in breadth and length…

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

Opens mid-sentence, completing s.12. Psalm 22:5 LXX = Psalm 23:5 English (ἐλίπανας, 'you made rich/anointed'). Psalm 127:3 LXX = Psalm 128:3 English. Palladius's quotation joins John 6:51 ('I am the living bread that came down from heaven') with John 6:33 ('gives life to the world'); cited as John 6:33, 51. 'Not all those from Israel have believed' and the olive imagery may echo Romans 9:6, 10:16 and 11:17–25; left uncited as doubtful. 'Greeks' (Ἑλληνικῆς) means the pagan nations, as often in Cyril. ἀσήπτων = 'that does not rot' (LXX for acacia wood). In Exodus 27:2 Cyril's text has καλύψεις αὐτά ('cover them'), plural, where the Hebrew has the altar; kept as 'them'. 'Crown' (στεφάνη) and 'cover' (καλυπτήρ) follow the LXX of Exodus 27:3 (Hebrew: pots and shovels). 'Of one piece with it' renders ἐξ αὐτοῦ ἔσται τὰ κέρατα ('the horns shall be from it'). The section ends mid-sentence at the PG column break.

changes: 'truer question' -> 'true question' (ἀληθῆ is positive, only ἐμφρονεστέραν is comparative)
'as the angel said' -> 'when the angel said' (genitive absolute, removes ambiguity)
Palladius's question reworded; κλῶνας rendered 'shoots' as distinct from κλάδοι
Articular infinitive τὸ ... κεῖσθαι rendered 'what is meant by the olive branches lying'
'you speak rightly' -> 'you are right'; 'what belongs to it' -> 'the things on it' (τῶν ἐν αὐτῇ)
Citations checked: Zechariah 4:14, Psalm 22:5 LXX = Psalm 23:5, Psalm 127:3 LXX = Psalm 128:3, John 6:33, 51, Exodus 27:1–3
